m:hallgrim: From September the church is open every day from 10am to 5pm and the tower from 10am to 4:45pm (last entry). In summer the hours are 9am–8pm. On Sundays the church and tower usually close from about 10:30am to 12:30pm for Mass; on weekdays the nave sometimes closes for private services. Tower: 1,500 kr (about €11) for adults, 1,300 kr with a student card, 200 kr for children aged 7–16. Tickets are bought in the church shop and can't be booked. Closed on 24 and 25 December and 1 January (official website).
m:harpa: The building is open Sunday to Tuesday from 10am to 6pm and Wednesday to Saturday from 10am to 8pm; the foyer is free, while concerts, exhibitions and guided tours have separate tickets (prices on harpa.is: not read). The box office is open every day from 10am to 6pm. The Sun Voyager is on the seafront and can always be seen, for free.
m:laugavegur: Free to walk. Shops are usually open from 10am to 6pm (Saturday until 5pm, Sunday reduced hours or closed); cafés stay open into the evening. In October and November it gets dark early, by around 6pm, and the streets fill with lights.
m:tjorn: Free to walk. The cathedral (Dómkirkjan) is usually open during the day, with reduced hours at weekends (not checked). The City Hall has a foyer with a large relief model of Iceland, which according to guides can be visited during office hours (not checked).
m:landnam: Open every day from 10am to 5pm. Entry 1,800 kr (about €13) for adults, 1,150 kr for students, free up to age 17. Closed on 24, 25 and 26 December, 31 December and 1 January (City History Museum website).
m:hofn: Free to walk, but whale-watching and puffin trips (seasonal) are booked separately and depend on the weather; in winter departures are less frequent (prices and times not read). The harbour venues have their own hours.
m:hafnarhus: Open Friday to Wednesday from 10am to 5pm and Thursday from 10am to 10pm. Closed at Easter, 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January; on 26 December it opens from 1pm to 5pm. One ticket covers the city's three art museums (I didn't read the price: check on listasafnreykjavikur.is).
m:thjod: Open every day from 10am to 5pm. Entry 3,300 kr (about €24) for adults, 1,600 kr for students and seniors, free under 18 (museum website). The café is currently closed.
m:perlan: Adult ticket 7,090 kr online (about €52), 7,490 kr at the desk; children aged 5–12 5,090 kr. The ticket has an entry time chosen when you buy it. The hours I found don't match (the official website says 10am–6pm with last entry at 5pm; other sources 9am–9pm): book ahead and check perlan.is. The restaurant is closed. From the centre: Strætó bus (line 18 stops at Perlan: check in the app).
m:laugardal: Open on weekdays from 6:30am to 10pm and at weekends from 8am to 10pm (City Council website). I didn't read the entry price: check on reykjavik.is. Before getting in the water you must shower without a swimsuit, as the rules at the entrance require; bring a towel or hire one.
vd:pylsur: Iceland's most famous hot dog stand, near the harbour, open since 1937: the classic order is «eina með öllu», a hot dog with everything, meaning raw and fried onion, ketchup, sweet mustard and remoulade. Eaten standing on the pavement.
vp:pylsur: A hot dog cost about 500–600 kr (about €4) in one guide, but the price has probably gone up (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:messinn: A fish restaurant near Lækjartorg, known for its fish pans served sizzling at the table: cod, salmon or fish of the day with potatoes and butter. A small, warm and very popular place.
vp:messinn: Upper-mid range: a fish dish is usually around €25–35 (menu not seen). Hours from a May 2026 listing, to be confirmed.
vd:svarta: A place on Laugavegur that serves soup in a bread bowl: reindeer soup or a creamy herb soup is served inside a freshly baked loaf. Generous portions and a cosy setting, with works by local artists.
vp:svarta: A bread-bowl soup usually costs around €18–25 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:mokka: Reykjavík's first café, open since 1958, with walls covered in paintings and a quiet atmosphere; it brought espresso to Iceland. Famous for its cakes and hot chocolate.
vp:mokka: A coffee with a slice of cake is around €10–13 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:sandholt: A historic Reykjavík bakery on Laugavegur: sourdough bread, butter croissants and pastries, slices of cake and hot breakfasts. Eat at the little tables or take away.
vp:sandholt: A coffee and a croissant are around €8–10; a full breakfast around €15 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:loki: A café serving traditional Icelandic food opposite Hallgrímskirkja: steamed rye bread with mashed fish or smoked lamb, and rye bread ice cream. An honest choice for trying local flavours at sane prices.
vp:loki: A typical dish is around €14–20 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:roasters: A small roaster with coffee roasted on site, a short walk from Hallgrímskirkja: shared tables, good filter coffee and pastries. Often full.
vp:roasters: A coffee is around €4–6 and a pastry €5–7 (menu not seen). Hours from a 2020 guide, to be confirmed.
vd:thrir: A family-run restaurant since 1989, specialising in fish: cod, haddock and Icelandic specialities like dried fish, with some whale and seabird dishes you can avoid. It has a cheaper lunch menu on weekdays.
vp:thrir: Mid-range: a main course is around €25–35; lunch costs less (menu not seen). Hours from the Visit Reykjavík website, to be confirmed.
vd:haiti: A café with Haitian and Ethiopian cooking at the old harbour: freshly brewed coffee, stews and fish soup, in a warm, colourful setting. It opens early in the morning.
vp:haiti: A coffee and a cake are about €8–10; a hot dish €15–20 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:kaffivagninn: The harbour fishermen's café, open since 1935: a big breakfast, fish soup and home-style dishes at popular prices, frequented by workers and fishermen.
vp:kaffivagninn: Breakfast around €12–16 and a hot meal around €15–25 (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:hlemmur: Reykjavík's first food hall, in a former bus station: a dozen counters with lamb, Neapolitan pizza, ramen, sandwiches and a bar at one end. Get your food and sit at the shared tables.
vp:hlemmur: A meal from a counter is around €14–22 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
cd:whales: A gallery of life-size whales, at the harbour.
cd:avvistamento: Three hours by boat from the city, with the chance to see whales and dolphins.
cx:avvistamento: The tour leaves from the Old Harbour.
cd:harpatour: The concert hall with the coloured-glass façade.
cd:kjarval: The museum of Kjarval, the painter of lava landscapes, in Klambratún park.
cd:aurora: A museum about the Northern Lights, where you learn how auroras work.
cd:flyover: A simulated flight over waterfalls and glaciers, on a moving seat.
cd:phallo: A curious museum, with specimens of every Icelandic animal.
cd:skylagoon: A geothermal lagoon by the sea, a few kilometres from the centre.
cx:skylagoon: It's in Kópavogur, about 5 km from the centre.
cd:maritimeis: The history of fishing in Iceland, with a coastguard ship to visit.
